response.answer: Put batch-processing mornings first. You’ve described thriving with protected, sustained-focus work: checkpointed batch reconciliations stayed accurate at high volume, and quiet time let you clear backlog. By contrast, frequent interruptions are especially draining, and open-desk conversation is costly because of your hearing; you explicitly said rare true emergencies are manageable but “the drumbeat” is not. The drop-in help window can still be a secondary choice, particularly if questions are scheduled or batched, which you find pleasant and cleaner. This recommendation is based on the work patterns and hearing-related constraint you described, not on any broader assumptions.
